Covilhã''', is a Portuguese [[association football|football]] club from the city of [[Covilhã]] that plays in the third-tier [[Liga 3 (Portugal)|Liga 3]]. The club was founded on 2 June 1923 and became the branch number 8 of [[Sporting CP|Sporting Clube de Portugal]] (Sporting CP).{{Cite web |title=Filiais do Sporting |url=https://www.dn.pt/dossiers/desporto/sporting/as-casas-do-sporting/filiais-do-sporting-1004270.html/ |access-date=2024-02-29 |website=Diário de Notícias |language=pt |archive-date=2024-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240220105816/https://www.dn.pt/dossiers/desporto/sporting/as-casas-do-sporting/filiais-do-sporting-1004270.html/ |url-status=live }} Their nickname is the ''Leões da Serra'', meaning "Lions of the Mountain Range," due to Covilhã's location in the [[Serra de Estrela]], the highest mountains in Portugal. Their home ground is [[Estádio Municipal José dos Santos Pinto]], located at approximately 900 m of altitude{{Cite web |last=TheSportsDB |title=Sporting da Covilhã - Team Profile |url=https://www.thesportsdb.com/team/138855-sporting-da-covilh%c3%a3 |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=TheSportsDB |language=en}}. However, the team plays also at the newer stadium of [[Complexo Desportivo da Covilhã]], also in Covilhã, which holds a capacity of 3,000 spectators.{{Cite news |title=SC Covilhã estreia estádio renovado para dar melhores condições a jogadores e adeptos |url=https://www.ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20182019/noticias/geral/sc-covilha-estreia-domingo-estadio-renovado-para-dar-melhores-condicoes-a-jogadores-e-adeptos/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240921034639/https://www.ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20182019/noticias/geral/sc-covilha-estreia-domingo-estadio-renovado-para-dar-melhores-condicoes-a-jogadores-e-adeptos/ |archive-date=2024-09-21 |access-date=2025-08-01 |work=Liga Portugal}} Their current chairman is Marco Peba and current manager is Francisco Chaló. They have won five [[Portuguese Second Division|Second Division]] in 1948, 1969, 1987 (second-tier), 2002, and 2005 (third-tier). They have competed in the [[Portuguese First Division]] 15 times, and in the [[Portuguese Second Division]] 11 times (1948–49, 1958–59, 1986–87, 1996–97, 1999–00, 2002–03, 2005–06, 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2011–12)."}}
